title: fix(transport): bind SSE sessions to caller identity
author: vadim2404
body:
Prevents cross-channel response routing in the SSE transport. mcp-handler routes POST /api/message payloads to the SSE owner's process via Redis pub/sub keyed only on sessionId, with no ownership check — any caller who learns or guesses a live sessionId can inject messages into the victim's SSE stream, causing tool results to land on the wrong channel.

Adds two defenses:

1. POST-side ownership check (evaluateMessageOwnership): on POST to /message?sessionId=..., verify the caller's identity fingerprint matches the binding written to Redis when the SSE connection was established. Mismatch -> 403. Redis unreachable -> 503 (fail closed).

2. SSE-side envelope check (shouldRejectEnvelope): defence in depth. Each tool and prompt handler compares the caller identity carried through the envelope against the identity captured at SSE-connection setup, and refuses the invocation on mismatch. Catches any misrouted envelope that bypasses the edge check.

Identity = sha256(accountId:apiKey).slice(0, 32) — strict binding so that the same account presenting a different bearer still cannot inject into a peer's SSE.

Bindings live in Redis under mcp:session:${sessionId} with a TTL of maxDuration + 70s. SESSION_STARTED writes, SESSION_ENDED releases.

Tests: 32 unit tests (mocked redis), 9 integration tests against a real Redis instance covering round-trip, mismatch, unknown-session, TTL expiration, and evaluateMessageOwnership pass/403/unbound paths.

title: fix(npm): the packed tarball could never install — SHA256SUMS prefix mismatch
author: linhdmn
body:
## The bug

Before treating #86 as "just add a token", I packed the tarball from `main` and installed it. It fails for everyone:

```
npm error command sh -c node bin/install.js
npm error Installing db-mcp-server v1.13.0 for darwin-arm64...
npm error Failed to install db-mcp-server: no SHA-256 checksum found for db-mcp-server-darwin-arm64
```

A name mismatch between the two halves of the same release:

| Producer | Line | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `npm-publish.yml` → Build release binaries | `sha256sum release/db-mcp-server-* > release/SHA256SUMS` | `2ba669ff…  release/db-mcp-server-darwin-arm64` |
| `bin/install.js` → `findChecksum` | `if (name === asset)` | compares bare `db-mcp-server-darwin-arm64` |

Every manifest entry carries a `release/` prefix, the installer compared the whole field, so it throws **before downloading anything**. Both halves landed together in #88 (`bin/install.js` doesn't exist at v1.12.0), so no release of this package has ever been installable — the version on npm, if it ever gets published, would install for nobody.

Why it shipped: `npm-publish.yml` only ran `npm pack --dry-run`, which checks the tarball's *contents*, never its *behaviour*.

## The fix

- `bin/install.js`: `findChecksum` matches the basename as well (`name.split("/").pop() === asset`), keeping the existing binary-mode `*` marker handling. The top-level `install()` call is now behind `require.main === module` and the helpers are exported, so the parser is testable without triggering a download.
- `bin/install.test.js` (new, 8 cases): prefixed entry, windows `.exe`, bare name, `*` marker, digest lowercasing, blank/comment lines, genuinely-absent asset, wrong-architecture-of-same-platform (must still throw).
- `npm-publish.yml`: `node --test bin/install.test.js` in the `verify` job, plus an **end-to-end smoke step** in `publish-npm` — pack the tarball, `npm install` it, run `db-mcp-server --help`. That is the check whose absence let this ship.
- `.gitignore`: un-ignore `bin/install.test.js` (the `!/bin/install.js` allowlist needed the new entry).

## Verification

- **RED first**: all 8 new tests fail against the unfixed parser with the exact production error (`no SHA-256 checksum found for db-mcp-server-darwin-arm64`).
- **GREEN**: `node --test bin/install.test.js` → `# pass 8`, `# fail 0`.
- **End to end against the real v1.13.0 release**: `npm pack` → `npm install` succeeds; the postinstall downloads the darwin-arm64 binary and its SHA-256 `2ba669ff…` matches the published `SHA256SUMS` entry exactly; the installed launcher runs (`db-mcp-server --help` prints usage, exit 0).
- `actionlint` on the modified workflow: no findings beyond the pre-existing style notes. `node --check` passes on both launchers.
- Not published by accident: `package.json` `files` lists explicit paths, so `npm pack` still contains exactly 7 entries and `bin/install.test.js` is not among them.

Docs updated in this PR: `docs/cycles/cycle-61-npm-install-checksum.md` (+ INDEX row) and the PRD distribution section.

**Unchanged:** npm publishing is still blocked on `NPM_TOKEN` (#86). What changes is that the first real publish will now produce a package that installs.

title: fix: handle literal  string when env var is unset
author: vchomakov
body:
## Fix: Handle literal `${REDIS_URL}` string when environment variable is unset

### Problem
When the `REDIS_URL` environment variable is not set, gemini-cli passes the raw `"${REDIS_URL}"` string as the `--url` parameter instead of omitting it or passing an empty value. This causes the Redis MCP server to attempt parsing the literal string `"${REDIS_URL}"` as a Redis URI, which fails with a parsing error.

### Root Cause
The issue occurs because:
1. gemini-cli constructs command line arguments that include `--url ${REDIS_URL}`
2. When `REDIS_URL` is unset, shell expansion doesn't occur, so the literal string `"${REDIS_URL}"` gets passed
3. The server tries to parse this as a valid Redis URI, which fails

### Solution
Filter out the `"${REDIS_URL}"` placeholder string.
This allows the server to gracefully fall back to using individual Redis connection parameters (host, port, etc.) with their default values when no valid URL is provided.

### Impact

- Fixes Redis MCP server startup failures when installed from PyPI and used with gemini-cli
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing configurations
- No breaking changes to the API or configuration options

title: fix: Add connection pool keep-alive settings
author: echarrod

## Summary

Adds connection pool configuration options to prevent connection timeouts, especially useful for long-running connections or connections through proxies that may timeout idle connections.

## Changes

### Configuration Options Added
- `waitForConnections: true` - Queue connection requests when pool is full instead of immediately erroring
- `queueLimit: 100` (default, configurable) - Limits queued requests to prevent unbounded memory growth
- `enableKeepAlive: true` - Enable TCP keep-alive packets
- `keepAliveInitialDelay: 0` - Start keep-alive checks immediately
- `connectTimeout: 10000ms` (default, configurable) - 10 second connection timeout for better UX

### Environment Variables
- `MYSQL_QUEUE_LIMIT` - Override default queue limit (default: 100)
- `MYSQL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` - Override connect timeout in milliseconds (default: 10000)

## Use Cases

This addresses connection stability issues when:
- Running long-lived MCP server instances
- Connecting through proxies with idle connection timeouts
- Database servers behind load balancers or connection pools
- Network conditions with intermittent connectivity

## Code Quality

- ✅ CodeRabbit review passed with no issues
- ✅ Configurable via environment variables
- ✅ Sensible defaults to prevent resource exhaustion

## Testing

Tested with staging MySQL connection through proxy that times out idle connections after 1 hour. Keep-alive settings maintain stable connection.

### Problem

User-controlled inputs from `workflow_dispatch` (e.g., `version`) were directly interpolated into shell commands via `${{ github.event.inputs.version }}`, allowing arbitrary command execution on the GitHub Actions runner.

title: fix: reload TOML config per source instead of reconnecting every source
author: tianzhou
body:
Addresses problem 1 of #454 on its own, with no new surface. The runtime API and the other open questions on that issue stay open.

## Problem

On a `dbhub.toml` change the watcher called `connectorManager.disconnect()` on every source and then reconnected them all. In-flight queries finished, but until the slowest one did, every new call on every source failed with `Cannot use a pool after calling end on the pool`, including sources the edit never touched. The reporter measured 18 of 80 calls failing on an untouched source while another source was added.

## Change

The reload is now a diff against the last applied source list (`applySourceDiff` in `src/utils/config-watcher.ts`):

- Unchanged sources are left alone and keep their pools.
- New sources are connected (or registered lazily), removed ones are disconnected, edited ones are reconnected, one source at a time.
- Rollback is per source. A changed source whose new config fails to connect is restored to its previous config. A new source that fails is skipped. Tools referencing a source that is not live are dropped from the registry, so one bad source cannot take the rest down.
- Source order follows the file, so the first `[[sources]]` entry stays the default.

`ConnectorManager` gains `addSource()`, `removeSource()` and `reorderSources()`. `disconnect()` is unchanged and still used at shutdown. The `initialTools` option on the watcher is gone since whole-config rollback no longer exists.

Docs: the hot reload section in `docs/config/toml.mdx` now describes the per-source behavior.

## Tests

- `src/utils/__tests__/config-watcher.test.ts` rewritten for diff semantics: unchanged sources untouched, add/remove/change, per-source rollback, failed new source skipped, reorder, successive reloads diff against the last applied state, tool filtering, debounce, invalid file keeps everything.
- `src/connectors/__tests__/manager.test.ts`: add eager, add lazy then connect on first use, duplicate id rejected, remove one leaves the other connected, remove unknown is a no-op, reorder changes the default.

`pnpm run build` and `pnpm test:unit` pass (39 files, 1112 tests).

linked_issues.title: Add or remove sources at runtime without reconnecting the others
linked_issues.body:
## Use case

We run one HTTP DBHub as a sidecar that serves several databases, and the set of databases changes while it runs. An admin registers a database in our control plane, and it should be queryable within seconds. Removing one should make its tools disappear. Neither should require restarting DBHub or editing a file on the host.

The TOML hot reload from #257 gets close. Our control plane could rewrite `dbhub.toml` and let the watcher pick it up. Two things get in the way.

## Problem 1: a reload disrupts every source, not just the changed one

On reload, the watcher calls `connectorManager.disconnect()` on all sources and then reconnects them all. In-flight queries finish, but until the slowest one does, every new call on every source fails with `Cannot use a pool after calling end on the pool`.

Measured on 1.3.1 with Postgres 16: source A was called every 100 ms while a 6 s query ran on it, and source B was added to the file mid-way. 18 of 80 calls on A failed. Source A was never touched by the edit.

## Problem 2: a file is an awkward interface for a control plane

To use the file, the caller needs a writable shared volume next to DBHub. In Kubernetes a ConfigMap update is a symlink swap, and `fs.watch` does not see it reliably. The caller also has to render TOML safely with credentials inside it, and serialize its own writes. An API next to the existing `GET /api/sources` would avoid all of that.

## What we prototyped

https://github.com/bytebase/dbhub/pull/452

title: fix(schema): Use sample instead of find for schema sampling
author: kmruiz
body:
## Proposed changes

Using find without sorting will return documents in natural order, which is not reliable for sampling because it depends on the last "updated" time a document was updated. By using find, we are biased towards the latest documents in a database that might not even be up to date, introducing bias.

The `$sample` works differently: it actually does an statistical sample by getting random documents from different random places within the same collection. This is more reliable on collections where not all documents have the same amount of fields.

title: Fix: make a failed AWS IAM refresh recoverable instead of losing the source
author: tianzhou
body:
## Summary

`refreshIamSourceConnection` deleted a source's connector before reconnecting it. When the reconnect threw (an expired SSO session is the common trigger), the connector was gone, the early-return guard skipped every later refresh tick, and every tool call against that source failed with a self-contradicting message until the process was restarted:

```
Source 'cardissuing' not found. Available sources: teller, token, cardissuing, ...
```

This makes the failure recoverable: the next tool call after the user re-authenticates reconnects transparently, and the error message no longer lists a source it refuses to use.

Closes #424

## Changes

- **Recoverable refresh** (`refreshIamSourceConnection`): if `connectSource` throws after the old connector has been torn down, hand the source back to `lazySources`. `ensureConnected` then retries it on the next tool call, surfacing the real error (e.g. the token-minting failure) while credentials are still bad, and reconnecting once they are valid again.
- **Timer re-arm** (`scheduleIamRefresh`): re-arm only while the source is still in `connectors`, instead of whenever it is in `sourceConfigs`. A source in the lazy state gets its timer back from `connectSource` on successful reconnect, so the process no longer spins a 14-minute timer that returns at the guard forever.
- **Accurate error message** (`ensureConnected` / `getConnector`): the "Available sources" list is now derived from sources that are connected or registered for lazy connection, rather than the append-only `sourceIds` list.

I went with the "make failure recoverable" option from the issue rather than the connect-first swap: `sshTunnels` and the refresh timer are keyed by source id, so building a replacement while the old one is alive would need `connectSource` split into build and register steps. This change is contained to the failure path.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests in `src/connectors/__tests__/manager.test.ts` drive the refresh timer with fake timers and a stubbed connector registry:
  - a refresh that fails on token minting leaves the source listed, `ensureConnected` retries and surfaces the real error, and reconnects once the token resolves; rotation resumes afterwards
  - the refresh timer stops re-arming for a source that is no longer connected
  - a source that can neither serve nor reconnect is not listed as available
- [x] All three new tests fail against the previous `manager.ts` and pass with this change
- [x] `pnpm test:unit`: 38 files, 1005 tests pass
- [ ] Field verification against an SSO-authenticated setup (the reporter offered to test a patch)

linked_issues.title: IAM source refresh deletes the connector before reconnecting; a failed refresh loses the source permanently
linked_issues.body:
### Summary

`refreshIamSourceConnection` deletes a source's connector **before** reconnecting it. If the reconnect throws — an expired SSO session is the common trigger — the source is left permanently unreachable for the life of the process, and every later tool call fails with a message that contradicts itself:

```
Source 'cardissuing' not found. Available sources: teller, token, transaction, txn_history, cardissuing, dw, ...
```

The named source appears in both halves of the sentence. That is the tell, and it's what makes this hard to recognise in the field — it reads like a config error rather than a dead connector.

Only restarting the MCP server recovers it.

### Mechanism

All line numbers are `src/connectors/manager.ts` on `main`.

**1. Delete-then-connect** — [`refreshIamSourceConnection`, :494](https://github.com/bytebase/dbhub/blob/main/src/connectors/manager.ts#L494):

```ts
const existingConnector = this.connectors.get(sourceId);
if (existingConnector) {
  await existingConnector.disconnect();
  this.connectors.delete(sourceId);      // <-- removed first
}
...
await this.connectSource(source);        // <-- if this throws, nothing puts it back
```

**2. The guard then makes the loss permanent** — the same function's early return (`:496`):

```ts
if (this.isDisconnecting || !source.aws_iam_auth || !this.connectors.has(sourceId)) {
  return;
}
```

Once the connector is gone, `connectors.has(sourceId)` is false, so every subsequent refresh returns immediately. T

title: fix: restore the mcp-server-neon user agent on SDK requests
author: andrelandgraf
body:
## Problem

Since 2026-07-22 17:00 UTC, the Neon control plane has not been attributing this server's traffic to MCP. Requests per day in `prod.transformed_marts.fact_segment_api_events`:

| Date | MCP requests | MCP distinct users |
|---|---|---|
| Jul 21 | 567,330 | 14,815 |
| Jul 22 | 400,128 | 12,603 |
| Jul 23 | 19,957 | 587 |
| Jul 28 | 20,174 | 583 |

A 96% drop in *distinct users* overnight is not usage. Combined `MCP` + `API` distinct users is flat straight across the boundary — 26,161 on Jul 21, 26,523 on Jul 22, 25,630 on Jul 23, 25,463 on Jul 28 — and the `API` + `oauth` action mix after the cutover is a copy of the `MCP` + `oauth` mix before it:

| action | MCP/oauth before | API/oauth after |
|---|---|---|
| database_info | 32,191 | 33,626 |
| projects_list | 7,260 | 8,793 |
| org_get | 7,574 | 8,088 |
| current_user_info | 6,952 | 7,201 |
| branch_create | 1,333 | 1,256 |

Same requests, different label. The cost is that MCP is no longer measurable: usage, adoption, and the backend error rate, which is the only reliability signal this server has because its own telemetry emits no error event.

## Diagnosis

`4614b0b` ("refactor: migrate MCP server to Neon SDK", #293) was authored 2026-07-22 10:08 PDT — 17:08 UTC, inside the hour of the cutover. It replaced a client that set the header on every request:

```ts
createApiClient({
  apiKey,
  baseURL: NEON_API_HOST,
  headers: { 'User-Agent': `mcp-server-neon/${pkg.version}` },
});
```

with one that sets nothing:

```ts
createSdkClient({ apiKey, baseUrl: NEON_API_HOST, throwOnError: true });
```

`@neon/sdk` sends no user agent of its own — `rg -i user-agent` across `node_modules/@neon/sdk/dist` returns zero hits — so requests went out with undici's default. Confirmed over real HTTP against the pre-fix code: a tool call's request arrives with `user-agent: node`.

**The two auth buckets moved differently, and that difference is what pins this to a deploy of this repo.** Splitting the `MCP`-labelled series by `auth_method`:

| Date | oauth requests | token requests | token users |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jul 21 | 63,814 | 503,516 | 11,848 |
| Jul 22 | 45,024 | 355,104 | 10,225 |
| Jul 23 | 0 | 19,957 | 587 |
| Jul 26 | 0 | 16,490 | 443 |
| Jul 29 | 0 | 20,141 | 562 |

`oauth` goes to zero and stays there: everything the hosted deploy serves under OAuth lost its label in one step. `token` falls 96% and then holds flat at ~20k/day. That residual is ordinary control-plane traffic — `current_user_info`, `org_get`, `database_info`, `projects_list`, no telemetry endpoints — so it is not a surviving code path inside the hosted server, which has exactly one deployed copy of this code. It is the population a deploy cannot reach: older locally installed copies of the package, which authenticate with an API key and still carry their own baked-in header.

So the bucket that survived is precisely the un-deployable one. A change in client behavior cannot produce that shape; a single deploy of this repo can, and did.

## The fix

`@neon/sdk`'s `NeonConfig` accepts `apiKey`, `throwOnError`, `waitForReadiness`, `wait`, `retries`, `baseUrl`, `fetch`, and `orgId`. There is no `headers` or `userAgent` option, and there deliberately won't be — see [neon-pkgs#362](https://github.com/neondatabase/neon-pkgs/pull/362), which proposed one and was closed. Identifying your application is a Neon concern rather than something the SDK's published audience needs a first-class field for, and `fetch` already covers it:

```ts
const USER_AGENT = `mcp-server-neon/${pkg.version}`;

const fetchAsMcpServer: typeof fetch = (input, init) => {
  const request = new Request(input, init);
  request.headers.set('User-Agent', USER_AGENT);
  return fetch(request);
};

const neon = createSdkClient({
  apiKey,
  baseUrl: NEON_API_HOST,
  throwOnError: true,
  fetch: fetchAsMcpServer,
});
```

**The header has to be added to the request, not supplied alongside it.** The SDK builds a `Request` — auth, content type, body — and calls `_fetch(request)` with no second argument. Passing `init.headers` therefore does not merge with anything; it replaces the entire header set, dropping `Authorization`, and every call 401s. Constructing from `(input, init)` and then setting the one header preserves whatever the SDK put there and still handles the `(url, init)` shape.

One wrapper covers every call. `resolveConfig` builds a single `client` from the config, and both the ergonomic resource namespaces (`neon.projects.get`) and raw calls (`raw.createProject({ client: neon.client })`) go through it.

Nothing changes for callers. `createNeonClient(apiKey)` keeps its signature, and no tool handler changes.

## Also in here

- The literal `` `mcp-server-neon/${pkg.version}` `` was written out in three places. It is now the `USER_AGENT` constant, used by the wrapper and by the raw request path.
- The third place was the facade's `userAgent` getter, which has no callers — every `.userAgent` in the repo is `ServerContext`'s or `authInfo.extra`'s, which carry the MCP *client's* agent, a different thing. Removed rather than rewired.

## Verification

Base `5de2555`. `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm fmt:check`, `pnpm knip`, and `pnpm build` clean. `pnpm test:unit` 376 passed, `pnpm test:integration` 102 passed / 9 skipped.

The test drives real MCP tool calls over the in-memory transport with `NEON_API_HOST` pointed at a loopback server that records what arrived. `NEON_TELEMETRY_API_HOST` derives from it, so one server serves both hosts:

- **`create_branch`** — the `POST /api/v2/projects/proj-1/branches` arrives with `mcp-server-neon/<version>`, still carries `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, and its JSON body is intact. Covers the SDK client.
- **`query_logs`** — the `GET /telemetry/v1/projects/…/loki/api/v1/query_range` arrives with both headers. Covers the raw escape hatch, which is separate code to a separate host.

Each was confirmed red for the right reason by mutating the fix:

| mutation | failure |
|---|---|
| drop `fetch: fetchAsMcpServer` — the regression itself | `create_branch`: `userAgent: "node"` |
| wrapper passes `init.headers` instead of setting on the `Request` | `create_branch`: `authorization: undefined` |
| drop the explicit header from `request()` | `query_logs`: `userAgent: "node"` |
| telemetry client calls `fetch` itself instead of the escape hatch | `query_logs`: `userAgent: "node"` |

The last row is why this asserts at the tool-call boundary and not on `createNeonClient`. What regressed is what the server puts on the wire while serving a tool call; a test that constructs the client itself passes that mutation while attribution silently breaks, and it would equally pass a future handler that builds its own SDK client — which is the shape of the change that caused this.

Not verified against production: nothing outside the control plane exposes what user agent it recorded. **The signal to watch after deploy is the `oauth` bucket of `MCP`, which is currently a hard zero and should return to 45–65k requests/day within a day.** Watch that rather than the `MCP` total, because the total also contains the ~20k/day from old local installs that this PR does not touch. If `oauth` stays at zero, the classifier keys on something other than the user agent and this diagnosis is wrong.

## For your attention

- **This wrapper is now the pattern for any Neon tool built on `@neon/sdk` that wants its traffic attributed, and the naive version of it is wrong.** Both versions typecheck; the difference is only visible in what reaches the wire:

  ```
  naive wrapper    {"ua":"my-cli/1.0.0"}                        <- Authorization gone
  correct wrapper  {"ua":"my-cli/1.0.0","auth":"Bearer k"}
  ```

  The failure is at least loud — dropping auth 401s every call immediately — but the next tool to do this will hit it. The `Authorization` assertion exists because the first version of this PR had that bug.
- **~20k requests/day of `MCP` traffic comes from old local installs and is outside our control.** Roughly 500 users a day, flat, on published versions that predate the migration. Nothing we deploy changes their header, and they are the reason the `MCP` total never went to zero. Worth knowing before anyone reads a recovery number off the total.
- **Other Neon-owned SDK consumers still send `node`.** `neonctl` and the rest of `neon-pkgs` have the same gap this PR closes for MCP, and nothing prompts them to fix it.
- **This runs on the Node.js runtime, which is what makes the fix work.** No route sets `export const runtime`, so the App Router default applies and undici lets `User-Agent` be set. Moving any Neon-calling path to the edge runtime would silently drop the header and reintroduce this bug, with no test failure unless that test also runs on edge.
- **Historical data is not backfillable and the series is not comparable across 2026-07-22 17:00 UTC.** Rows before it are correct; rows after undercount MCP by ~96%. Any 28- or 56-day window spanning that boundary will report a collapse that did not happen, for as long as the window includes it.

title: fix(pg-meta): pair composite FK columns positionally to avoid cartesi…
author: anp0429
body:
### What kind of change does this PR introduce?

Bug fix: data-integrity issue in `list_tables` (verbose) foreign-key output.

### What is the current behavior?

For any composite (multi-column) foreign key, `list_tables` (verbose) returns the **cartesian product** of the source and target columns. An N-column FK produces N² `foreign_key_constraints` entries instead of N : reporting column pairings that do not exist in the schema.

Repro:

```sql
create table public.parent (a int not null, b int not null, primary key (a, b));
create table public.child (
  a int not null, b int not null,
  constraint child_parent_fk foreign key (a, b) references public.parent (a, b)
);
```

`list_tables` with `verbose: true` returns 4 constraints for `child_parent_fk`:

```
public.child.a => public.parent.a
public.child.a => public.parent.b   <- does not exist
public.child.b => public.parent.a   <- does not exist
public.child.b => public.parent.b
```

Only `a=>a` and `b=>b` are real. Because this tool exists so an AI agent can reason about database structure, the fabricated relationships are silently trusted - an agent could infer key relationships that don't exist.

Root cause is in `pg-meta/tables.sql`. The FK subquery joins source and target columns independently:

```sql
... on sa.attrelid = c.conrelid  and sa.attnum = any (c.conkey)
... on ta.attrelid = c.confrelid and ta.attnum = any (c.confkey)
```

`any(conkey)` against `any(confkey)` cross-joins every source column with every target column, instead of pairing them positionally.

### What is the new behavior?

Each foreign key is now returned as **one constraint object** with the grouped shape discussed in the review below:

```json
{
  "name": "child_parent_fk",
  "source_table": "public.child",
  "source_columns": ["a", "b"],
  "target_table": "public.parent",
  "target_columns": ["a", "b"]
}
```

- Columns are walked in lockstep with `unnest(conkey, confkey) with ordinality`, so wrong pairings are impossible by construction, and both arrays aggregate ordered by constraint ordinality - `source_columns[i]` pairs with `target_columns[i]`, in constraint-definition order (not attnum, not alphabetical).
- `source_table` is kept in the output because `relationships` includes constraints where the listed table is the referenced target.
- Single-column FKs are emitted as one-element arrays for a uniform shape.
- Adds a regression test using deliberately non-alphabetical column order (`foreign key (b, a) references parent (y, x)`) so any future regression to attnum or name ordering fails immediately.

### Additional context

The same `pg-meta` query backs the schema-docs work in #278, so this fix helps that path as well.

title: fix: cache completed ClickHouse health results for one second
author: mosya415
body:
Fixes #227.

Rebased onto main and trimmed to the caching work, as asked in review. #152 already handles the event-loop blocking, the shared in-flight probe, the two second bound and client reuse, so none of that is in this PR anymore. What is left is the one piece the probe still lacks.

`/health` now caches the outcome of a completed probe, success or failure, for one second and answers from it. The existing probe path is untouched: the check still runs on `HEALTH_EXECUTOR`, concurrent requests still join one in-flight future, `_bounded_health_config` still clamps the driver timeouts, the two second wait is unchanged, the cancellation shield is unchanged, and `_claim_health_probe_log` still logs once per probe. The cache sits in front of `_get_health_probe_future` and only short-circuits when a completed result is still inside the window.

Single-flight covers concurrent probes; the cache covers sequential ones. An orchestrator polling `/health` once a second previously ran a ClickHouse check on every poll, because each poll arrived after the previous probe had finished.

Only completed results are cached, which matters for the timeout path. A request that gives up at two seconds caches nothing, since there is no result yet. The probe it left running caches its own outcome when it finishes, so the shield keeps its meaning, and a cancelled future caches nothing. Cached failures do not log again, so an unreachable ClickHouse under a probe storm writes one log line per probe rather than one per request.

The cost is that a failure or a recovery can be reported up to a second late. That is in the README health check section, in the route docstring, and in the changelog entry.

`tests/test_health_cache.py` adds 7 tests: reuse of a cached result within the window for both success and failure; a fresh probe past the window, including a failed backend that comes back reporting `200` again; a cached `503` with the same body bytes and the connection error logged once rather than once per request; 50 concurrent requests after a cached result opening no new probe, and 20 concurrent requests during an in-flight probe still sharing a single `HEALTH_EXECUTOR.submit` whose result is then cached; and a request that times out leaving the cache empty while the probe runs on, with the late completion caching its result. Setting `_HEALTH_RESULT_CACHE_SECONDS` to `0` turns 5 of the 7 into failures, so they exercise the cache rather than the probe.

`tests/conftest.py` clears the cache around every test. Without it a cached result leaks into the next test in `tests/test_optional_chdb.py`, which calls `health_check` several times in a row well inside one second.

`uv run ruff check .` passes. `uv run pytest -q tests` goes from 621 to 628 passing with an identical set of pre-existing failures, the ones that need a live ClickHouse.

Left the failed-construction pool manager leak alone, since you are taking it upstream in clickhouse-connect.

linked_issues.title: Bound and coalesce the public ClickHouse health check
linked_issues.body:
## Problem

`GET /health` is public by design for orchestrator probes. The async route directly calls synchronous `create_clickhouse_client()` on the ASGI event loop. Each request performs full ClickHouse client initialization with the normal 30 second connect and 300 second receive timeouts.

There is no health-specific timeout, cache, or single-flight. Concurrent probes run serially on the event loop, create redundant clients, and successful clients are not explicitly closed. Failed construction can also retain ClickHouse Connect pool managers.

This is pre-existing availability and resource hardening. PR #226 preserves the public health route for probe compatibility.

## Proposed fix

- Keep the current `200 OK` / generic `503` readiness contract.
- Run the synchronous ClickHouse check off the event loop.

title: fix: discourage host-filesystem access in raw-SQL tool descriptions
author: stoallan
body:
## What

Appends a shared `HOST_BOUNDARY_NOTE` to the descriptions of the two raw-SQL tools — **`execute_sql`** and **`apply_migration`** — and a matching one-line reminder in the server `instructions`, discouraging the model from reading server-side files or running OS commands via SQL (`COPY … FROM '/path'`, `COPY … FROM PROGRAM`, `pg_read_file`, `pg_ls_dir`, `lo_import`).

## Why

Cut **tripwire noise on the managed fleet.** LLMs driving the MCP attempt host-filesystem reads via SQL, and the tripwire fires on the **attempt** — it records that the SQL ran, not whether it succeeded — so every probe generates alert noise regardless of outcome. Discouraging the model from making the attempt reduces the volume at the source. This is the exfil-OUT counterpart to the injection-IN guidance already present (AI-794 / `wrapWithUntrustedDataBoundary`).

## Design

- **On the tool descriptions, not only `server` instructions.** Per the 2026 MCP spec, `instructions` rides on the *optional* `server/discover` response and isn't guaranteed to be injected; a client cannot invoke a tool without ingesting its description — so the description is the reliable delivery vehicle. The server-instructions line is added too, as opportunistic defense-in-depth.
- **Both raw-SQL tools.** `apply_migration` forwards arbitrary SQL too; these two are the only raw-SQL entry points.
- **A shared constant** (`HOST_BOUNDARY_NOTE`) to keep the two descriptions from drifting, mirroring the existing `wrapWithUntrustedDataBoundary` factoring.
- **Deployment-neutral wording.** The text names no deployment context — it's true everywhere. This matters because the same `mcp-server-supabase` also ships to self-hosted Studio, where a "Supabase-managed infrastructure" rationale would be false (the operator owns the host). No self-hosted benefit is claimed; the goal is purely managed noise.

## FYI (per review)

ChatGPT snapshots/freezes MCP tool descriptions + instructions, so this needs a plugin resubmission to take effect there — tracked on the Supabase side, no action here.

## Testing

String-concat append to two tool descriptions + one instructions bullet (type-trivial). No test asserts the raw-SQL description text (the `untrusted user data` assertions target the result wrapper), and the instructions test compares against the exported constant, so it stays in sync. Local suite not run — CI validates format/typecheck/tests.

title: fix(analytics): send clientApplication on tool_call events
author: andrelandgraf
body:
## Problem

`server_init` carries both `clientName` and `clientApplication`. `tool_call` carries only `clientName`. In `prod.transformed_marts.fact_segment_mcp_server_events` the consequence is absolute — over Jul 24–30, on the remote transports:

| transport | event | rows | missing `client_application` |
|---|---|---|---|
| stream | server_init | 1,043,012 | 0 |
| stream | tool_call | 1,043,005 | 1,043,005 |
| sse | server_init | 8,969 | 0 |
| sse | tool_call | 19,341 | 19,341 |

The 1:1 pairing on `stream` is not a coincidence and not sessions-to-calls: every streamable-HTTP request builds a fresh server instance with its own `hasTrackedServerInit`, so `server_init` fires once per request, alongside the `tool_call` from that same request. `server_init` on that transport counts requests, not connections.

Which sharpens what the null column costs. The two rows of a single request disagreed about whether the client was identifiable: one said `v0`, the other said nothing. `WHERE client_application = 'v0'` returned every one of those requests and none of the tool calls inside them, so v0 read as a client that arrives constantly and never does anything. The data is recoverable only by knowing to join on the raw `client_name` string (`'v0bot'`) instead, which is exactly the kind of thing a normalized column exists to avoid.

## The fix

Three code paths emit `tool_call`, and all three were missing the property that `server_init` already sends.

**Authenticated remote** (`app/api/[transport]/route.ts`) and **in-memory** (`mcp/server/index.ts`) are one line each. `clientApp` is already computed and already in scope — `getAuthContext` returns it, and the tool handler receives it as `extraArgs.clientApplication`:

```ts
const properties = {
  authMethod,
  tool_name: tool.name,
  readOnly: String(readOnly),
  projectScoped: String(!!grant.projectId),
  clientName: cName,
  clientApplication: clientApp,   // added
  traceId,
};
```

**Anonymous docs-only** (`?category=docs`) is the one that needed plumbing. It bypasses OAuth entirely, so there is no `verifyToken` to hang the User-Agent off an auth context the way the authenticated path does, and its `clientName` is the hardcoded string `'anonymous-docs'`. The header on the request carrying the tool call is the only client signal available, and it does reach the handler — `extra.requestInfo.headers` is populated by `mcp-handler` on this path, which the integration test asserts rather than assumes:

```ts
function readUserAgent(extra: { requestInfo?: RequestInfo }): string | undefined {
  const header = extra.requestInfo?.headers['user-agent'];
  return Array.isArray(header) ? header[0] : header;
}
```

`clientApplication` there is `detectClientApplication(userAgent)`, the same normalizer the other two paths use. On that path no raw User-Agent reaches analytics — only the normalized value — because `clientName` stays `'anonymous-docs'` and the `context` object passed to `track` is `{ app: docsOnlyAppContext }` and nothing else. That is a property of the docs path alone: on the authenticated path `clientName` *is* the raw User-Agent whenever the handshake supplied no name, and it goes up in both `properties.clientName` and `context.clientName` as it already did.

No event other than `tool_call` changes.

## Effect on the warehouse

`client_application` becomes non-null on every `tool_call` emitted by the two paths that reach production. `createMcpServer` in `mcp/server/index.ts` has no production caller — there is no `bin` entry, no `StdioServerTransport` in the repo, and the route uses `createMcpHandler` — so its rows are zero today. The line is there to keep the two implementations' telemetry contracts from drifting, and the e2e assertion exists to keep it there.

**`client_application` on `tool_call` now spans two populations.** Authenticated tool calls and anonymous docs fetches land in the same buckets, so `WHERE client_application = 'v0'` returns both. `docs_only` separates them and does so retroactively: the flag and the docs-only handler landed in the same commit (`af14c7c`, #230), so there is no window where a docs row lacks it.

```sql
-- tool calls by client, authenticated traffic only
select client_application, count(*)
from prod.transformed_marts.fact_segment_mcp_server_events
where event = 'tool_call'
  and docs_only is distinct from 'true'   -- 'true' only on the anonymous ?category=docs path
group by 1
```

Docs rows also carry `anonymousId = 'anonymous-docs'` and no `user_id`, so anything counting distinct users per `client_application` drops them silently rather than reporting them as anonymous.

This PR ships no backfill. A query spanning the deploy needs a date floor, or `detectClientApplication` applied to the raw `client_name` the older rows do carry — and that recipe works only on authenticated rows. Docs rows have `client_name = 'anonymous-docs'`, which the detector maps to `unknown`, so including them produces a series that jumps from `unknown` to real client names at the deploy and reads as a change in client mix that never happened. Exclude them with the filter above.

Values are the existing closed set from `detectClientApplication`: `cursor`, `claude-code`, `claude-desktop`, `v0`, `vscode`, `unknown`.

## Also in here

- `mcp/__tests__/mcp-server.e2e.test.ts` gains a module mock: `vi.mock('../analytics/analytics')` with a hoisted `trackSpy`, which forces the static `import { createMcpServer }` to become a hoisted `await import`. That file previously mocked nothing at module level. It is the highest-confidence suite in the repo and it no longer exercises the real analytics module — `track` and `flushAnalytics` are stubs for every test in the file, not only the new one. The alternative was leaving the `mcp/server/index.ts` line uncovered, which is what the first version of this PR did.
- `withConnectedClient` in the same file takes a `clientName` parameter, defaulted to the previous hardcoded `'test-client'`, so the new test can connect a client the detector recognizes. Every existing test is unaffected.
- `runDocsTool` takes a `userAgent` parameter and both docs-only `registerTool` callbacks take the `extra` argument they previously ignored. Tool names, descriptions, input schemas, annotations, responses, and the `handleToolError` path are untouched.

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm fmt:check`, `pnpm knip` clean. `pnpm test:unit` 376 passed, `pnpm test:integration` 104 passed / 9 skipped, `pnpm test:e2e:mcp` 7 passed. Base commit `da127d3`.

Behaviours now covered, each confirmed red before its fix and red for the missing key alone:

- a `tools/call` over streamable HTTP with `User-Agent: v0bot` emits **both** `server_init` and `tool_call` with `{ clientName: 'v0bot', clientApplication: 'v0' }`
- an unauthenticated `?category=docs` `tools/call` with the same User-Agent emits `tool_call` with `{ docsOnly: 'true', clientName: 'anonymous-docs', clientApplication: 'v0' }`
- the in-memory server, driven by a real MCP client over `InMemoryTransport` whose handshake `clientInfo.name` is `v0bot`, emits both events with the same attribution

The in-memory assertion exists because the route test alone left `mcp/server/index.ts` free to be reverted with the suite still green.

Also verified live with `mcporter` against a local server on `:3031` holding a real org-scoped API key, driving a full `create_project` → `list_projects` → `run_sql` → `delete_project` lifecycle in the disposable smoke org, from three clients with different User-Agents. The tracked `properties` object is the same reference passed to `logger.info` and to `track()`, so the emitted log line is the payload:

```
tool_call create_project  clientName=v0bot                        clientApplication=v0
tool_call list_projects   clientName=v0bot                        clientApplication=v0
tool_call run_sql         clientName=v0bot                        clientApplication=v0
tool_call run_sql         clientName=Cursor/3.13.10 (darwin arm64) clientApplication=cursor
tool_call list_projects   clientName=node                          clientApplication=unknown
```

The smoke project and the API key were deleted and revoked after the run.

Not verified live: the docs-only path was exercised only through the integration test against the real route handler, not against a deployed `?category=docs` endpoint. The warehouse table itself was not re-queried on this branch; the row counts above are the pre-fix state.

## For your attention

- **`docs_only` stays a `'true'`-or-absent flag; the two authenticated sites do not start emitting `'false'`.** Adding it would make the column two-valued going forward and unusable across the deploy — `docs_only = 'false'` would return only post-deploy rows, reintroducing the discontinuity this PR exists to remove. The absent-means-authenticated convention is correct over the whole history. Write the filter as `docs_only is distinct from 'true'` rather than `docs_only is null`: if someone later does add `'false'` to the authenticated sites, the null form silently starts dropping authenticated rows, which is a wrong answer with no error.
- **On streamable HTTP the MCP handshake `clientInfo` never reaches analytics.** Each request builds a fresh server instance, so `oninitialized` sets `clientName` on the instance that served `initialize` while `server_init` and `tool_call` are tracked on the instance that serves `tools/call`. Attribution on that transport comes entirely from the HTTP `User-Agent` fallback. It works — v0 sends `User-Agent: v0bot` — but the comment on `oninitialized` describing `clientInfo` as the more reliable source is not true for the transport that carries essentially all traffic, and any client whose User-Agent is a generic runtime string lands in `unknown` no matter what it declares in the handshake. Not addressed here.
- **The docs-only slice of `client_application` is unverified self-report.** `?category=docs` is publicly documented in `public/llms.txt` and needs no credentials, so any caller can send `User-Agent: v0bot` and land in the `v0` bucket. The authenticated paths are only marginally better; nothing decision-bearing should hang on the anonymous slice.
- **The property set is still built independently in three places, and `client_application` is the second divergence, not the first.** `customScopes` is on `server_init` and on neither `tool_call`, so tool calls by scope still require a nearest-timestamp join per user — the fragile recovery the Problem section condemns. Constructing the set once would prevent the third; it is not done here because it would restructure three handlers to fix a one-line data bug.
- **This does not make the column safe to group on retroactively.** Anything querying `client_application` on `tool_call` before the deploy still gets null, and this PR ships no backfill.

title: fix(auth): stop embedding grant in OAuth state + migrate headers to URL query params
author: andrelandgraf
body:
## Summary

### 1. Fix: Stop embedding grant context in upstream OAuth state

PR #199 introduced grant context (scope categories, read-only mode, project-id scoping) as an MCP-layer concept. However, it accidentally embedded the grant context into the `state` parameter that gets forwarded to the Neon console OAuth backend. The downstream auth server does not understand these MCP-specific scopes — it must remain unaffected.

This PR reverts all changes to the upstream OAuth redirect URL so it is identical to what it was before #199. Grant context was previously resolved from saved registration headers in the `/callback` route instead — this is now superseded by the query param migration below.

### 2. Feat: Migrate X-Neon-* headers to URL query params

Encoding grant context directly in the MCP server URL query params has several advantages over the previous `X-Neon-*` header approach:

- **Config travels with every request** — no staleness when users change their MCP config
- **No need for custom HTTP header support** in MCP clients (many clients don't support custom headers)
- **Query params are the natural way to configure an HTTP endpoint** — matches how other MCP servers work (e.g. Supabase)
- **Changes take effect immediately** — no re-auth or re-registration needed

#### New URL format

```
https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp?readonly=true&category=querying&category=schema&projectId=proj-123
```

#### Priority for read-only mode

1. `readonly` query param (new, highest priority)
2. `x-read-only` header (legacy, kept for backwards compat)
3. OAuth scope (existing, read-only if scope is `read` only)
4. Default: `false`

#### Priority for grant context (categories + projectId)

1. URL query params `category` and `projectId` (read at transport time)
2. Stored token grant from OAuth flow (fallback for existing tokens)
3. Default: `DEFAULT_GRANT` (full access, no project scoping)

### Files changed

**Core:**
- `grant-context.ts` — Replaced `resolveGrantFromHeaders` with `resolveGrantFromSearchParams` + `mergeGrant`
- `read-only.ts` — Replaced `neonHeaderValue` with `queryParamValue`, updated priority chain

**Transport & routes:**
- `[transport]/route.ts` — `verifyToken` reads query params from URL. OAuth path merges URL grant with stored token grant. API key path uses URL grant directly.
- `list-tools/route.ts` — Switched to query-param-based grant/read-only resolution
- `register/route.ts` — Removed `X-Neon-*` header logging and CORS entries
- `authorize/route.ts` — Simplified `defaultReadOnly` to only use `x-read-only` header
- `callback/route.ts` — Stores `DEFAULT_GRANT` (transport-time params override at runtime)
- `grant-filter.ts` — Updated warning messages to reference query params

**Tests:**
- Unit: `grant-context.test.ts`, `read-only.test.ts`, `list-tools-endpoint.test.ts`
- Integration: `oauth-authorize-route.integration.test.ts`, `oauth-register-route.integration.test.ts`
- E2E: `list-tools.spec.ts`, `mcp-response-integrity.spec.ts`, `oauth-register-authorize.spec.ts`

**Docs:**
- `README.md` — New "URL Query Params for Access Control" section with examples
- `SMOKE_TESTS.md` — Enhanced multi-phase agent-driven smoke test plan

The MCP Server falls back to default values `neondb` and `neondb_owner` when no database and role_name is provided from LLM while invoking the tool. The Server blindly assumes that the database with the name `neondb` and role with the name `neondb_owner` exists in the project. 

This PR does two things

- Completely removes the default `neondb_owner`, and always use `database.owner_name` when no explicit role name is provided. If LLM provides a non-existing role, the tool will fail as expected
- If no database is provided, the server now looks for a database named `neondb` and uses that. If it does not exist, it uses the first available database.

title: fix(tools-atlas): declare mcp-metrics and mcp-types as runtime deps
author: gagik
body:
## What
`@mongodb-js/mcp-tools-atlas` ships a `dist` that imports `@mongodb-js/mcp-metrics` and `@mongodb-js/mcp-types` at runtime (e.g. `dist/mockMetrics.js`, `dist/tools/connect/connectCluster.js`, `dist/helpers/sharedTierAlertsHook.js`) but only declares them in `devDependencies`. This breaks strict (`hoist=false`) consumers like `10gen/mms`, which currently has to work around it with a `packageExtensions` override injecting both packages.

## Why
Move `@mongodb-js/mcp-metrics` and `@mongodb-js/mcp-types` from `devDependencies` to `dependencies` so the published package declares its actual runtime dependencies. Consumers can drop the override once this is released and re-resolved.

title: Fix: Resolve symlinks in main module detection
author: addamx
body:
# Fix: Resolve symlinks in main module detection

## Problem

When the script is executed via a symlink, `path.resolve()` doesn't resolve the symlink, causing `isMainModule()` to incorrectly return `false`.

## Solution

Replace `path.resolve()` with `fs.realpathSync()` to properly resolve symlinks to their actual file paths before comparison.
